description: Establish the rebuild foundation: confirm the CI-only verification reality, add the new immersive dependencies to package.json AND package-lock.json in sync, widen the CSP in src/server.ts to admit the sources a WebGL/3D + smooth-scroll layer needs (blob: workers, data:/blob: images for canvas textures, wasm), and lay down the design-token + shared-utility groundwork (a design tokens layer in src/styles.css, a src/lib/motion.ts with prefers-reduced-motion + WebGL-capability + client-mount helpers). This feature adds NO visual behavior on its own; it makes the later features installable, type-correct, CSP-clean, and SSR-safe by construction. Everything here is a prerequisite for FEAT-002 through FEAT-005.
steps: Confirm the environment baseline WITHOUT trying to fix it: run `ls node_modules/.bin` and a single `npm ci --dry-run` (or note the 403) to CONFIRM (not repair) that tool binaries are absent and the npm registry is unreachable under INTEGRATIONS_ONLY. Record in findings that typecheck/lint/test/build cannot run locally and must be validated by CI. Do not retry installs.

Add the immersive dependencies to package.json `dependencies` with correct, mutually compatible version ranges for React 19: `three`, `@react-three/fiber` (v9, React 19 compatible), `@react-three/drei` (v10, R3F v9 compatible), and a lightweight smooth-scroll library `lenis` (formerly @studio-freight/lenis). Add `@types/three` to devDependencies. Do NOT add a separate large animation lib unless a later feature needs it; the CSS scroll-driven + IntersectionObserver + rAF approach already in the repo plus R3F's useFrame is sufficient. Keep the dependency set minimal and justified.

Update package-lock.json so `npm ci` will succeed in CI: add the new top-level packages and their transitive dependencies to the lockfile with resolved URLs/integrity consistent with the chosen version ranges. If a fully correct lockfile cannot be produced by hand in-sandbox, still add the packages.json entries and CLEARLY note in findings that CI's `npm ci` requires the maintainer/CI to regenerate package-lock.json (e.g. run `npm install` once with network). Prefer producing a correct lockfile; a broken/partial lockfile that fails `npm ci` is worse than a clearly-flagged note.

Widen the CSP in src/server.ts minimally for the new client-side 3D/motion layer while keeping it strict: keep everything same-origin, but ensure `worker-src 'self' blob:` remains (already present), add `blob:` to `img-src` (canvas/WebGL readback and drei helpers can create blob URLs), add `data:` where a shader/texture may inline, and add a `wasm-unsafe-eval` source to `script-src` ONLY IF a chosen dependency needs wasm (three core does not; document the decision either way). Do NOT loosen to `unsafe-eval` or add third-party hosts. Add a comment explaining each new source and that all 3D assets remain bundled same-origin.

Add a shared client-capability + motion utility module at src/lib/motion.ts exporting: `prefersReducedMotion()` (SSR-safe, returns false on server), a `useReducedMotion()` React hook that subscribes to the media query, a `useIsMounted()`/`useHasMounted()` hook for client-only gating, and a `supportsWebGL()` capability check (SSR-safe, feature-detects a WebGL2/WebGL context, returns false on server or on failure). All functions must guard `typeof window`/`document` for SSR and be lint/type clean.

In src/styles.css, introduce a clearly-delimited design-token block (extending the existing :root tokens, not replacing them) for the immersive system: spatial/elevation tokens, motion-duration and easing tokens, z-index scale for the 3D canvas vs content vs cursor, and a reduced-motion global guard (@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) that neutralizes transitions/animations for the new classes). Preserve all existing tokens and the self-hosted @fontsource imports untouched.
Do NOT modify generated files (src/assets/images.ts, src/routeTree.gen.ts). Do NOT alter src/lib/forms.functions.ts, submission-guards.ts, or their tests in this feature.
acceptance_criteria: package.json dependencies include three, @react-three/fiber, @react-three/drei, lenis, and devDependencies include @types/three, all with React 19-compatible version ranges.
package-lock.json is either updated in sync with package.json (preferred) OR findings explicitly state CI must regenerate the lockfile with network access; the situation is unambiguous.
src/server.ts CSP is widened only for same-origin blob:/data:/wasm sources actually needed by the 3D layer, with an explanatory comment per added source, and no third-party host or unsafe-eval added.
src/lib/motion.ts exists and exports SSR-safe prefersReducedMotion, useReducedMotion, a client-mount hook, and supportsWebGL, all guarding window/document.
src/styles.css contains a new immersive design-token block plus a prefers-reduced-motion guard, with all pre-existing tokens and font imports intact.
No generated files (images.ts, routeTree.gen.ts) and no form/guard logic were modified.
The code is written to be type-correct and prettier/eslint clean by construction (cannot be run locally).
verification: Run `ls node_modules/.bin` and confirm the absence of tool binaries is documented, not that a fix was attempted.
Read package.json and package-lock.json and confirm the new deps are present and (preferably) in sync; if not in sync, confirm findings flags it for CI.
Read src/server.ts and confirm the CSP changes are minimal, same-origin, and commented.
Read src/lib/motion.ts and confirm every window/document access is SSR-guarded.
CI (npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test && npm run build) is the authoritative validator and must pass after the maintainer resolves the lockfile if it could not be produced in-sandbox.
findings:
ENVIRONMENT (confirmed, not repaired): Network mode is INTEGRATIONS_ONLY. `node_modules/.bin` does not exist at all (ls returns 'No such file or directory'), so there are NO tool binaries (vite/tsc/eslint/vitest). npm itself is unusable in-sandbox: even `npm ci --dry-run` and plain `node -e` abort with 'Cannot find module /opt/amazon/kiro-agent/proxy-bootstrap.js' (a broken NODE_OPTIONS preload) before touching the registry, so installs cannot be run or retried here. CONSEQUENCE: typecheck, lint, test, and build CANNOT run locally; all code was written type-correct and prettier/eslint-clean by construction and MUST be validated by CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml: typecheck -> lint -> test -> build). JSON validity of package.json and this file was confirmed with python3.

DEPS ADDED to package.json: dependencies += three ^0.180.0, @react-three/fiber ^9.1.0 (v9 = React 19 compatible), @react-three/drei ^10.0.0 (v10 = R3F v9 compatible), lenis ^1.1.20 (smooth scroll, successor to @studio-freight/lenis). devDependencies += @types/three ^0.180.0 (matches three minor). No extra animation lib added; repo's IntersectionObserver + rAF + R3F useFrame + lenis are sufficient.

LOCKFILE — ACTION REQUIRED BY CI/MAINTAINER: package-lock.json was NOT modified. A correct lockfile cannot be produced by hand in this sandbox because the registry is unreachable, so the resolved URLs, integrity SHAs, and full transitive dependency tree (three, R3F, drei's large peer set, lenis) are unavailable. The feature guidance states a broken/partial lockfile that fails `npm ci` is worse than a clearly-flagged note, so package-lock.json is intentionally left in sync with the PRE-existing deps only. CI uses `npm ci`, which WILL FAIL against the current lockfile until it is regenerated. To fix: run `npm install` once with network access (e.g. locally or in a network-enabled CI step) to regenerate package-lock.json in sync with the updated package.json, then commit it. This is the single blocking item for CI green; everything else is complete.

CSP (src/server.ts): widened minimally, same-origin only. Added blob: to img-src (canvas/WebGL readback + drei generated textures create object URLs); worker-src 'self' blob: already present and its comment extended to cover WebGL worker use. NO wasm source added (three core ships no WebAssembly and no draco/basis decoders are pulled in; decision documented in the header comment). NO unsafe-eval, NO third-party hosts. Each change carries an explanatory comment.

MOTION UTILS (src/lib/motion.ts, new): exports prefersReducedMotion() (guards window/matchMedia, false on server), useReducedMotion() hook (starts false for hydration parity, subscribes to the media query), useHasMounted() + useIsMounted alias (client-only gating), supportsWebGL() (guards document, probes webgl2/webgl/experimental-webgl, false on server or failure). All DOM access SSR-guarded.

STYLES (src/styles.css): added an additive immersive-system token block inside :root (z-index scale --z-canvas/content/sticky/overlay/cursor, motion durations --motion-instant..slowest, easings --ease-immersive/emphasized/spring, spatial depth + elevation tokens) without touching any existing token or @fontsource import. Extended the existing @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block with a guard neutralizing animation/transition/transform for [class*="immersive-"] elements. No generated files (images.ts, routeTree.gen.ts) and no form/guard logic touched.
